sections.content: How many people are "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters"?

24,630 people

were counted on the census as "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters investigate and write up stories and features for broadcasting and for newspapers, magazines, news websites and other periodicals.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters", 15.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters" included:

  • social and humanities scientists
  • teachers of english as a foreign language
  • civil engineers

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters" there were a similar number of men and women (53.5% compared with 46.5%).

This means "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 53.5% and women made up 46.5% of "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters" included:

  • public relations and communications directors
  • debt, rent and other cash collectors
  • shelf fillers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters", 10.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (71.2% compared with 28.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (57.7%) than self-employed (42.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Lambeth, this is in the same region of London.
